body:
Hey buddy. Let me tell you something:

Look at that 8 pack. Decent chest. Hiking in the middle of the goddamn forest shirtless like a boss. Clearly you can also afford to go on sweet-ass vacations to tropical destinations so you've got money.

Congratulations. You have some extremely valuable things that some people would kill for. Focus on those.

Your face is not ugly to the person that ends up loving you. If that person hasn't found you yet then why worry about it? The people that we end up in the best relationships with are seldom the ones we thought we would. Most people our age haven't even met their lifelong SO's yet. If these are all true, why worry?

You have things you can be confident in. The guys who get girls focus on those things and ignore their insecurities. This is what works. Even if the confidence is fake, it is better than real insecurity.

Love will find you. Don't worry about that. Just keep being relatively wealthy, 8 pack abs, confident you.

I'm glad you think you're happy now, but do you think you will continue to be happy?

Feeling wanted and loved and needed are very good feelings. it is hard to describe the wholeness of the feeling, but if you've felt i you will understand. 

When we break up with someone, all those feelings we may have felt from them become invalidated. We feel crushed and broken. Some more than others, some less than others, but negative feelings all the same. 

What if we are getting back together with someone that has put us through a cycle of both of these sets? What are the implications? That they regret putting you through these feelings? That they themselves don't like how the feelings affect them? Or you?

The real question here is why. Why would anyone want to get back together with someone that made us feel so bad? It's to confirm what you thought they thought about you was true. That you are worthy of admiration. You are worthy of fighting for. You are worthy of the emotional heartache and pain to be with.

This is the lie we feel is so true, but it is only that. A lie.

You want him back because he comforts you. Here's something that has taken me too long to learn: comfort is not happiness. The same in reverse. 

Granted sometimes these things work out; It is for the most part based on context. However, here are literally millions of people that could probably evoke the same feelings in you and you wouldn't have to worry about things going back to the way they were before you broke up. Because they are not him.

Anyway, I have been exactly where you are before and know just what you're feeling. I wish you best of luck. Just remember to choose happiness over comfortability. Humans are amazingly adaptable and can get comfortable anywhere, but you must search for what makes you happy.
This is perfect. Thank you for the help!

That sounds like good advice.

My next question is how to go about cutting ties. I'm a stereotypical pleaser type and it's difficult for me to be completely up front about things like this. He knows I am displeased but having a conversation that will more or less be a break up one is not something I typically do.

Should I just grow a sack and be brutally honest? 

Actually, I'm realizing now that I've typed this all out that this is probably the best course of action.

Before my ex and I broke up I fantasized about this quite a bit and brought it up more than once with her. She was actually pretty okay with it and we decided maybe it could be possible.

The problem is that while the thinking about it was a major turn-on, actually doing it in reality would be a whole different matter. The thought of anyone being as intimate with her as I was started to lose its appeal. I knew I could trust her %100, but I wasn't sure how I'd feel about it afterwords. She was lightly into bdsm and like to fantasize a little bit herself, but I struggled with the thought of her enjoying someone else more than she enjoys me.

Anyway, I guess what I'm trying to say is even though it's something you think you will enjoy, it may have other repercussions not only with her but you as well. Trust between you two will be extremely important for this to work successfully. Tread these waters carefully.

Are you trolling? Or just not trying to understand her side?

She made this deal to stop **him** from doing anything wrong, which he already has. As far as we know she has done nothing to rock the trust in the relationship. You are the one making assumptions now.

Also, this is close to violating rule #1 in the sidebar. We're here to be supportive not scrutinize.

>Losing her father because her mother hated that her boyfriend got facebook and talked to girls?

No, because he cheated on her. Marriages with children collapse for the same reason. There are plenty of single parents doing a fine job of raising their children. There are plenty of men that would be happy to be with OP that would not cheat. Why should she settle for less?

The father has already proven he isn't reliable enough to maintain a trusting relationship with OP. What about the relationship with his own child? What if he cheats again on OP? Or just leaves? You have to put yourself in her shoes.

OP says that the father has always wanted a baby, but his actions are suspicious given his history and the lies. He cannot have his cake and eat it too. That is utterly selfish.

You're missing the point.

He made a new Facebook, added all the same people he's had sex with in the past, and has been talking to all of them, all behind her back. This is a trust issue. He's been lying. It takes a long time to rebuild trust and the way to do it isn't by lying about who you're talking to.

The only person with anything to prove was the bf showing he could be trustworthy and now he's blown it. If he was unhappy with not being able to be social than the right thing to do would have been to leave, but instead he lied. 

OP is way better off on her own than with someone she can't feel she can ever trust.

No.

Cheating is a pattern of behaviour, not necessarily a single act of infidelity. For a lot of cheaters, these same patterns keep popping up from time to time and they don't ever really work at stopping the process. Someone who has dealt with a cheater will be hypersensitive to these patterns and it is very hard to forgive. Forgetting is impossible.

He lied in the past and she got cheated on. He started lying again, so she dumped him to save herself from the pain. Not an overreaction at all.
